idiom_name: one uniform indentation step per level, delimiters aligned, compound bodies on their own line
implementation_notes: Language-neutral recipe: give every nesting level exactly one indentation step; open a block's delimiter at the end of the statement that owns it (or on its own line, per the local style) and close it aligned with that statement, so the two delimiters read as opposite corners of a rectangle; put a compound body on its own indented line while a single simple statement may share the header line. Then treat the rectangle as a budget rather than a decoration: when the shape would overrun the width limit, extract a named step (Composed Method) or reject the case early (Guard Clause) instead of adding another level. Hand the actual rendering to the project's formatter and check it in CI - the convention survives when a tool enforces it, not when a reviewer asks for it.
code_sketch:
if (!input.isValid())        # guard clause: exit before the body
    return default_result    # ... so the normal path stays one level deep

value = compute(input)       # compound work stays at one level
total = value + offset
return total
pitfalls: Delimiters not aligned with the statement that opened the block: the rectangle reads as a ragged edge and the nesting level stops being countable.
Treating alignment as permission to nest: a perfectly aligned six-level body still hides its control flow; the shape exists to make depth visible, not acceptable.
Reformatting fragments inside a file that uses another style produces something that is neither the old shape nor the new one.

Wrong move: treat aligned delimiters as permission to keep nesting -> this fails because a perfect rectangle can still hide six levels of decisions -> instead extract a composed step or return early with a guard clause.

Wrong move: indent continuation lines like a nested block -> this fails because the eye reads a nesting level that the grammar does not execute -> instead use the formatter's continuation layout or introduce a named temporary.

Wrong move: run a formatter with changing width or style defaults on every touched file -> this fails because wrapping churn obscures behavior changes and damages blame -> instead pin the formatter configuration and isolate mechanical reformat commits.
